name: rtk-dangerous-actions-blocker
description: Deprecated: use block-destructive-commands, which shares this policy's destructive-command table. rtk#1007. Same table as block-destructive-commands: blocks root/home/.git deletes, force/delete/mirror pushes, reset --hard, clean -f, switch --discard, IaC destroy, cloud deletes, DB drops, lockouts; asks rm -rf off rtk's safe list, one named kubectl delete, bare lease, stash drop, prunes; dry-run flags pass. Own rows block credential-file reads (.env, keys, ~/.ssh) and echo or inline *_API_KEY/_SECRET/_TOKEN. Skips file rows in container exec. [Session-enforced in Codex by a PreToolUse hook: a matched command is denied before it runs (witnessed blocking on Codex Desktop, Windows, 2026-08-24; the deny is returned as hook JSON, not an exit code, which Codex's Windows shell wrapper mangles). Codex requires a one-time trust review per hook -- the plugin is ADVISORY until you approve its hook, and a plugin update voids that trust until re-approved. The hook needs git and a Python 3.11+ (python3, python or py) on PATH; with no working Python it exits 2 rather than allowing, and any other failure of the HOOK (missing git, a timeout, an unexpected exit) fails OPEN. A failure of the GUARD it runs is a DENY here, because Codex rejects the confirmation prompt the other clients get. Repo-wide enforcement at commit time and in CI still needs `chock sync`.]
